messages.content: Can you compare the Friday-to-Monday compact rental with using rideshares the whole time? Include parking and fuel, and I need a realistic plan for moving hotels Monday with our bags.

The all-rideshare estimate is $250 to $330 for the full stay. The rental starts at $284 including taxes, then adds $60 for three nights of La Jolla parking and about $35 for fuel. Because the car would be returned Monday, you would still need roughly $35 to $47 in rideshares from the rental return to Little Italy and from Little Italy to SAN on Wednesday. That puts the rental plan around $414 to $426 total.
So rideshares are cheaper by at least $84?

Yes. Comparing the high end of rideshares with the low end of the rental plan, the savings are about $84. At the other end, $250 in rideshares versus $426 for the rental saves about $176. The rental only becomes competitive if the $250 to $330 estimate omitted several longer local trips.
It includes the airport trips, Saturday dinner in Little Italy, and a couple of trips around La Jolla. We don't have anything planned far inland.

Then the all-rideshare plan is the better fit. It costs less, avoids the La Jolla parking charges, and removes the Monday rental-return deadline. The main variable is surge pricing, but even a $40 cushion above the current high estimate would leave it below the rental plan.
How should Monday work if La Jolla checkout is 11 and the Little Italy room might not be ready until 3? I don't want to drag luggage around for four hours.

Arrange luggage storage with the Little Italy hotel. Around 10:30 a.m., check out in La Jolla and request a rideshare directly to the second hotel. Aim to arrive around 11:00 to 11:30, leave both bags with the bell desk, and ask whether early check-in is available. If the room is not ready, spend the gap in Little Italy and return when the hotel messages you. That keeps the luggage out of the day without requiring a car.
Would it make sense to ask the La Jolla hotel to hold the bags instead?

Only if you want to remain in La Jolla until midafternoon. Otherwise, it creates an extra return trip to collect the bags before heading downtown. Moving the luggage to Little Italy at checkout is simpler and probably saves one rideshare.
Okay. Lay out the full transportation sequence through the Wednesday flight. That departure is still 5:35 p.m.

Friday after the 11:15 a.m. arrival, collect your checked bags and take a rideshare from SAN to the La Jolla hotel. Use rideshares for any local trips Friday through Sunday, including the Saturday 7:30 p.m. dinner in Little Italy and the return to La Jolla afterward. Monday, check out around 10:30 a.m., ride with the luggage to the Little Italy hotel, store it there if necessary, and check in after the room is released. Tuesday can be handled on foot in Little Italy with rideshares only as needed.
And Wednesday timing? Also give me the final transportation number separately from airfare and lodging.

For the Wednesday 5:35 p.m. nonstop departure, request the airport rideshare around 2:30 p.m.; that should put you at SAN near 2:45 to 3:00, leaving ample time to check bags. Final transportation choice: all rideshare, budgeted at $250 to $330, or $370 with a conservative surge cushion. Airfare remains separate at $1,142 plus the separate $140 checked-bag estimate. Lodging remains $2,018.46. Nothing is booked; confirm Monday luggage storage with the Little Italy hotel before committing to the split stay.
